Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown, velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may yellow and drop early.
organic_remedies: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to reduce spores for next season.
Prune the canopy so leaves dry quickly after rain.
Sulfur-based sprays during early leaf growth can protect new leaves.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides applied from green-tip stage are used for scab; ask your agriculture officer for an approved product and schedule.
prevention: Choose scab-resistant varieties when replanting.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves that grow into brown 'frogeye' lesions; fruit rots and shrivels into black mummies; cankers on branches.
organic_remedies: Prune out dead wood and cankers and burn or bury them.
Remove mummified fruit from the tree and the ground.
Keep the canopy open so foliage dries fast.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicide sprays from bloom through early summer are commonly used; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Disinfect pruning tools between cuts.
Keep trees well watered and fed to reduce stress.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, later with small tube-like growths underneath; fruit may be spotted.
organic_remedies: Remove nearby juniper or red cedar trees that carry the alternate stage of the fungus, where practical.
Remove and destroy badly infected leaves.
chemical_remedies: Fungicides are usually timed from pink bud to a few weeks after petal fall; confirm product and timing locally.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and shoot tips; leaves may curl, thicken or distort.
organic_remedies: Sulfur or neem-oil sprays at first sign can slow spread.
Prune to open the canopy and remove badly infected shoots.
Avoid excess nitrogen, which pushes soft growth that mildew prefers.
chemical_remedies: Several systemic and contact fungicides are registered for powdery mildew; ask your agriculture officer which one suits your stage and region.
prevention: Keep good airflow and avoid dense planting.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular tan to gray lesions running parallel to the leaf veins, mostly on lower and middle leaves first.
organic_remedies: Rotate with a non-cereal crop and bury or remove infected crop residue after harvest.
Avoid planting maize after maize in the same field.
Improve spacing and drainage to reduce long periods of leaf wetness.
chemical_remedies: Foliar fungicide is considered when lesions reach the upper leaves before tasseling; ask your agriculture officer about product and timing.
prevention: Choose hybrids with tolerance to gray leaf spot.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, round to oval, brick-red to brown powdery pustules on both sides of the leaf.
organic_remedies: Plant resistant or tolerant hybrids.
Plant early where possible, since late-planted crops are hit harder.
Scout regularly; mild infections often need no treatment.
chemical_remedies: Fungicide is only worth considering if rust is heavy on young plants; confirm with your agriculture officer.
prevention: Rotate crops and manage residue.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions, usually 2-15 cm, starting on lower leaves and moving up.
organic_remedies: Rotate crops and bury or remove infected residue after harvest.
Use resistant hybrids.
Avoid dense planting.
chemical_remedies: Foliar fungicide may be justified when lesions appear before or around tasseling; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and rotate fields.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan leaf spots with a dark border and tiny black dots; berries turn brown, then shrivel into hard black mummies.
organic_remedies: Remove mummified berries and infected canes during winter pruning.
Open the canopy with shoot thinning and leaf removal near fruit.
Copper or sulfur sprays can help in organic systems where permitted.
chemical_remedies: Protectant or systemic fungicides are used from early shoot growth to fruit set; ask for an approved schedule.
prevention: Keep vineyard floor clean and trellis vines for airflow.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellow or red-brown between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; wood shows dark streaks inside.
organic_remedies: There is no cure. Prune out infected wood during dry weather and burn it.
Protect pruning wounds with a sealant or wound protectant.
Remove vines that are severely affected so they do not infect neighbours.
chemical_remedies: No spray reliably cures esca; discuss wound-protection options with your agriculture officer.
prevention: Prune late in the dormant season and avoid large pruning wounds.
Plant clean, certified vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo; heavily affected leaves dry and fall early.
organic_remedies: Remove fallen leaves and infected foliage.
Improve airflow with canopy management.
Bordeaux mixture or copper sprays are traditionally used where permitted.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides are used during wet periods; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and over-crowded vines.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling of leaves that does not follow the veins evenly, small lopsided bitter fruit, and twig dieback.
organic_remedies: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected trees so the disease does not spread.
Control the Asian citrus psyllid insect that carries the bacterium, using yellow sticky traps and neem-based sprays on new flushes.
chemical_remedies: Insecticides targeting the psyllid are the main chemical tool; ask your agriculture officer for approved products.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock.
Report suspected cases to your local agriculture or horticulture department.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular dark spots on leaves that may fall out leaving 'shot holes'; sunken dark spots and cracking on fruit.
organic_remedies: Prune for airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.
Copper sprays during dormancy or early season can reduce spread where permitted.
Avoid excess nitrogen.
chemical_remedies: Bactericide programmes exist but control is partial; ask your agriculture officer about options.
prevention: Plant tolerant varieties and use clean planting material.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with a yellow edge; raised scabby spots on fruit.
organic_remedies: Remove and destroy infected plants and avoid working in the field when leaves are wet.
Copper-based sprays can slow spread where permitted.
Water at the base of plants rather than overhead.
chemical_remedies: Copper-based bactericides are commonly used; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed or seedlings.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for at least 2 years.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern) on older leaves first, often with yellowing around them.
organic_remedies: Remove badly infected lower leaves and destroy them.
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves.
Keep plants well fed and watered; stressed plants get blight more easily.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides are used on a regular schedule in wet weather; confirm product and dose with your agriculture officer.
prevention: Rotate crops for 2-3 years and use certified seed tubers.
Destroy volunteer potato and weed hosts.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked dark patches on leaves, with white fuzzy growth underneath in humid weather; stems and tubers can rot. Spreads very fast.
organic_remedies: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants away from the field.
Avoid overhead irrigation and irrigate early in the day.
Hill up soil to protect tubers and delay harvest until haulms are fully dead.
chemical_remedies: Late blight needs prompt fungicide protection in cool, humid weather; contact your agriculture officer urgently for product and schedule.
prevention: Plant certified seed tubers and resistant varieties.
Do not leave cull potatoes lying around the field.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on the upper surface of leaves and on stems; leaves yellow and dry out.
organic_remedies: Spray sulfur or neem oil at first sign, covering both sides of leaves.
Remove badly infected leaves.
Space plants widely for airflow.
chemical_remedies: Several fungicides are registered for powdery mildew on cucurbits; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Plant tolerant varieties and avoid crowding.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots on leaves that grow together; centres turn brown or gray and leaf edges look scorched.
organic_remedies: Remove and destroy infected leaves, especially after harvest.
Avoid overhead watering and do not over-crowd plants.
Renovate old beds and replace plants that are heavily affected.
chemical_remedies: Fungicides can be used during wet periods; ask your agriculture officer for an approved option.
prevention: Plant disease-free runners and resistant varieties.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves that may have a yellow halo; rough scabby spots on fruit.
organic_remedies: Remove infected plants and avoid handling plants when wet.
Copper-based sprays can slow spread where permitted.
Water at the base and use mulch.
chemical_remedies: Copper-based bactericides are commonly used with limited effect in heavy outbreaks; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and rotate crops for 2-3 years.
Clean tools and stakes between seasons.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, with yellowing around them; can spread to stems and fruit.
organic_remedies: Remove infected lower leaves and destroy them.
Mulch around plants and stake them to keep leaves off the soil.
Water at the base and avoid wetting leaves.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides are used on a regular schedule in humid weather; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Rotate crops for 2-3 years and clear plant debris after harvest.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy gray-green to brown patches on leaves, white mould underneath in humid weather, dark firm patches on fruit. Spreads very fast.
organic_remedies: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants away from the field.
Avoid overhead irrigation and improve airflow.
Do not compost infected plants.
chemical_remedies: Late blight needs prompt fungicide protection in cool, humid weather; contact your agriculture officer urgently for product and schedule.
prevention: Use resistant varieties and certified seedlings.
Keep potato and tomato plots apart where possible.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf surface with olive-green to gray velvety mould underneath.
organic_remedies: Lower humidity: increase ventilation, space plants and avoid wetting leaves.
Remove infected leaves and destroy them.
Water in the morning so leaves dry quickly.
chemical_remedies: Fungicides are used if humidity cannot be reduced; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Use resistant varieties, especially in polyhouses.
Clean greenhouse structures between crops.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with gray-white centres and dark edges, usually starting on lower leaves; leaves yellow and drop.
organic_remedies: Remove infected lower leaves and destroy them.
Mulch to prevent soil splash and stake plants.
Water at the base, not on leaves.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides are used from the first spots; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Rotate crops for at least 2 years and clean up debris after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckling on leaves, bronzing, and fine webbing underneath in hot dry weather.
organic_remedies: Spray leaves (especially undersides) with water to knock mites off.
Neem oil or insecticidal soap sprays reduce populations.
Encourage natural predators and avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill them.
chemical_remedies: Miticides are a last resort; ask your agriculture officer for a registered product and rotate modes of action.
prevention: Keep plants well watered in hot weather and control dusty conditions and weeds nearby.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and a yellow halo on leaves; can also spot stems and fruit.
organic_remedies: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
Stake and prune plants for better airflow.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
chemical_remedies: Protectant fungicides are used on a schedule in humid weather; confirm product and dose locally.
prevention: Rotate crops and avoid planting too densely.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges, plants are stunted, and flowers drop with little fruit set. Spread by whiteflies.
organic_remedies: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected plants early.
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, neem-based sprays and insect-proof nets on nurseries.
Remove weeds that host whiteflies.
chemical_remedies: Insecticides targeting whiteflies are the main chemical tool; ask your agriculture officer for approved products and rotation.
prevention: Plant virus-resistant varieties and use virus-free seedlings.
Use reflective mulch to deter whiteflies.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green patches on leaves, curled or fern-like distorted leaves, and stunted growth.
organic_remedies: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected plants.
Wash hands with soap and disinfect tools after handling plants.
Do not handle plants after using tobacco products.
chemical_remedies: No spray cures virus diseases; focus on hygiene and resistant varieties.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and resistant varieties.
Clear old plant debris and weeds and rotate crops.
